newsitem.title: USA: Times Mirror in pact to cut outstanding shares.
newsitem.headline: Times Mirror in pact to cut outstanding shares.

text.p: Times Mirror Co., publisher of the Los Angeles Times, said Friday it has entered into an agreement with its largest shareholder that will reduce the company's outstanding stock and boost earnings per share.

Under the two-part deal, Times Mirror and the Chandler Trusts will make equal capital contributions to form a limited liability company. Chandis Securities, a holding company principally owned by one of the Chandler Trusts, will then be merged into a subsidiary of Times Mirror.
Times Mirror said the transaction will reduce its outstanding series A common stock by six million shares and its outstanding 8 percent series A preferred stock by $367 million.
The deal will increase earnings per share in 1997 and add more than 10 cents per share to earnings in 1998, Times Mirror Chairman Mark Willes said in a statement.
"This reduction in common and preferred shares will enable us to achieve our target capital structure," he said.
In addition, Times Mirror will continue to use its active open market share repurchase programme to maintain this capitalisation, Willes said.
Los Angeles-based Times Mirror said it will contribute its real property with a market value of $226 million to the limited liability company, along with $249 million in cash.
The real estate will be then be leased back to Times Mirror under long-term leases, and the cash will be invested in a portfolio of securities of unrelated issuers.
The Chandler Trusts will contribute five million shares of the series A common stock valued at $254 million, and $221 million stated value of 8 percent series A preferred stock.
Under the transaction, Times Mirror will acquire 80 percent of the shares of the series A common stock contributed to the limited liability company, or about four million shares.

Times Mirror will also acquire 80 percent of the 8 percent series A preferred stock contributed, worth about $177 million. Due to the allocations, the dividends on such shares are effectively eliminated.
The merger will result in the reduction of the series A common stock by two million shares and the acquisition of $190 million stated value of 8 percent series A preferred stock.
Completion of the transaction is subject to approval by Times Mirror's board, which will meet to consider the transaction later Friday.

In addition to the Los Angeles Times, Times Mirror publishes Newsday, The Baltimore Sun and other newspapers; a wide array of professional information for the legal, health sciences, aviation and training markets and consumer magazines.
Times Mirror's stock rose 31 cents to $50.25 on the New York Stock Exchange in early afternoon trading.
